Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 95 (Indie)

fields.name: Beryl Slabs (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create eight plates of pure beryl at points within range of the spell. Each beryl plate is 6 inches thick and 10 feet tall by 10 feet wide. You can distribute the plates in any way you choose within range.
	The plates are perfect squares and can be placed in any position (horizontal or vertical). Any adjacent slabs merge with each other, and each plate can act as a foundation for another, allowing for continuous constructions in any direction, such as bridges or ramps, as long as at least one of the plates is anchored to the earth to be stable.
	A plate cannot occupy the space of a creature or object. If a plate appears in a location occupied by a creature, it is pushed to any side of your choice. If you try to trap a creature between the plates, the creature can make a Dexterity saving throw and position itself outside on a success.
	Each plate has an AC of 16 and 180 hit points, disappearing magically if reduced to 0, possibly causing the collapse of adjacent plates at the GM's discretion.
	As a bonus action, you can dispense the plates at any time during the spell. If you maintain concentration for the entire duration of the spell, you can choose to keep the plates permanently, but they will turn into plates of slightly greenish rock, without any value other than stone. If you choose not to keep the plates permanently or lose concentration before the end of the spell, the plates disappear magically without a trace.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can create two more slabs for each slot level above 5th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 8d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 95 (Indie)

fields.name: Blaze Light (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (an obsidian worth at least 50 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You cast a small spark at a point within range and then it explodes into a wave of confusion in a 10-foot-radius sphere. All creatures in the area must make a Wisdom saving throw or become extremely disoriented on a failure.
	An affected target can't take reactions and must roll a d10 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior for that turn.
	At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make a Wisdom saving throw. If it succeeds, this effect ends for that target.

Confusion Behavior:
d10 | Behavior
1 | The creature uses all its movement to move in a random direction. To determine the direction, roll a d8 and assign a direction to each die face. The creature doesn't take an action this turn.
2-6 | The creature doesn't move or take actions this turn.
7-8 | The creature uses its action to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach. If there is no creature within its reach, the creature does nothing this turn.
9-10 | The creature can act and move normally.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the radius of the confusion wave increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 4th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 96 (Indie)

fields.name: Blazing Army (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a ruby worth at least 500 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite all weapons of all allied creatures within a 30-foot radius sphere within range. For the duration of the spell, all natural and wielded weapons are considered magical and deal an extra 2d6 fire damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot radius sphere centered on you and deals 11d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 96 (Indie)

fields.name: Blessing of the Earth (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a handful of sacred soil)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create a square area immune to dispel magic, with a side of 60 feet, having one of the vertices at a point within the range of the spell.
	While within the area of the spell, all allied creatures, when making attack rolls and saving throws, can roll 1d4 and add the result to their roll, have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened, and any healing they receive within the area will consider results of 1 or 2 on the dice as 3. Hostile creatures within the area that make an attack or saving throw must roll 1d4 and subtract the value from the roll.
	Creatures within the area cannot be targeted by divination spells. The blessing also crosses planes, preventing any ethereal travel within the area and preventing extraplanar creatures from being summoned or conjured within the area.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 96 (Indie)

fields.name: Blossom (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You manifest a series of flowers in the space you occupy, which immediately grow and bloom, releasing their pollen in a circular area with a 20-foot radius centered on you. Any charm or frightening effect affecting a creature in the area ends immediately. Additionally, any creature hostile towards you or your allies within the area must make a Charisma saving throw, and on a failure, they become indifferent to you and your allies until the end of the spell or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw instead of Dexterity.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 96 (Indie)

fields.name: Burning Dash (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

When you cast this spell, a flame that rises from your feet covers your entire body, increasing your speed and strength momentarily. As part of this spell, you can immediately move 40 feet in any direction you choose. During this movement, you can push objects up to five times your normal capacity (or 150 times your Strength score in pounds). If you collide with a creature, the movement ends, and the creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 40 feet back and fall prone. If the creature's movement is interrupted by obstacles, it will fall prone and suffer 4d6 bludgeoning damage in addition. If the path is blocked by another creature, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, suffering the same damage and falling prone on a failure.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot radius sphere centered on you and deals 10d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 96 (Indie)

fields.name: Burning Eyes (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You cause the eyes of a creature within range to glow like blazing embers. During the spell's duration, the target gains proficiency with Charisma (Intimidation). If it already has this proficiency, the target doubles its proficiency bonus on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and those checks are made with advantage. Additionally, any creature that the target damages has disadvantage on its next attack roll against the target until the start of the target's next turn.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals fire damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 97 (Indie)

fields.name: Burst of Embers (HB)
fields.components: S, M (a special coal worth at least 5 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You magically create a glowing dust and blow it into a Burst of Embers that illuminates everything it covers. Any creature in the area that fails a Dexterity saving throw will be covered by this glowing dust for the duration of the spell. For the duration, covered creatures and objects shed dim light in a 10-foot radius. Any attack roll against a covered creature or object has advantage if the attacker can see it, and the affected creature or object can't benefit from being invisible.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals fire damage and on damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 97 (Indie)

fields.name: Call Allies (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You can bring your allies to assist you. When casting the spell, choose up to four willing creatures. As long as they are within 1 mile of you, each of these creatures can be teleported from their locations to an unoccupied space closest to you. If there isn't enough free space for the creature to be within 10 feet of you, or if you are somehow unreachable, the creatures will know they were called but won't be able to teleport.
	Objects carried by the creatures are teleported along with them, but other creatures that were being carried are not.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 97 (Indie)

fields.name: Calm Mind (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You fill your mind with the calm that only water can achieve. For the duration, you become immune to psychic damage, any effect that may sense emotions or read thoughts, divination spells and the charmed and frightened conditions. Optionally, you can transform the effect into an aura, affecting willing creatures of your choice within 20 feet of you, but you must concentrate to maintain the spell in this way. In this option, the spell will last only until the start of your next turn, ending sooner if you lose concentration.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot radius sphere centered on you and deals 12d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 97 (Indie)

fields.name: Circle of Protection (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a hand sized glass or crystal, that shatters when the spell ends)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You choose a point on the ground within range and then a large rune appears there, emitting a cylindrical mystical barrier with a 10-foot radius and 30 feet in height. No spell of 5th level or lower cast outside the barrier affects creatures or objects within it, even if cast At Higher Levels: Creatures within the area can be targeted by spells, but do not suffer their effects, and area spells have their effects suppressed within the cylinder.
	You can also, as a reaction, deflect a spell of 3rd level or lower cast against a target within the barrier. Then you choose another creature within range but outside the area to be the target. If you do so, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a slot of 7th level or higher, you block spells of up to 6th level and can deflect a spell of up to 4th level.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 10d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 6th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 97 (Indie)

fields.name: Commandment of Fire (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You point to a creature within range and place a magical command in its mind. The command forces the creature to perform some task or abstain from some action or to take a course of activity as you decide. The creature must understand you to be affected, and if it does, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for the duration. Whenever the charmed creature takes actions against its will, it takes 1 level of exhaustion, but no more than 1 level per day. A creature that doesn't understand you is immune to this spell.
	You can issue any command you choose, short of an activity that would result in certain death. If you issue a suicidal command, the spell ends.
	You can end the spell early by using an action to dismiss it. A remove curse, greater restoration, or wish spell also ends it.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 7th-level or 8th-level spell slot, the duration is 1 year. When you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, the spell lasts until it is ended by one of the spells mentioned above.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 98 (Indie)

fields.name: Compressed Air Image (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create an illusion of an object, creature, or other visible phenomenon as if you had cast the major image spell. But when the image is attacked or comes into contact with a creature, it explodes into a burst of air affecting a 20-foot radius sphere. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take 3d8 thunder damage, are deafened, and are thrown 80 feet in the opposite direction of the explosion. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw takes half damage, is not deafened, and is thrown 20 feet.
	A deafened creature must make a Constitution saving throw at the start of their turn, ending the deafened condition on a success. A thrown creature that has their movement impeded takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet they are unable to move. If they are obstructed by another creature, that creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the same damage on a failed save or no damage on a success.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 11d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 98 (Indie)

fields.name: Conjure Earth Guardian (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small figurine encrusted with gems worth at least 100 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You conjure an earth guardian, with the same appearance as the figurine used, that emerges from the ground in an empty 10-foot cube. Use the stat block of an earth elemental to characterize the guardian, which will remain for the duration of the spell or until reduced to 0 hit points, disappearing magically when the spell ends.
	The guardian obeys you to the best of its ability and acts after you in the initiative order. You can give simple courseof-action commands, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action. If you want to give a command the size of a phrase, you must spend a bonus action. If you lose concentration, the guardian will continue to follow the last command until completed. If the guardian completes the action and cannot hear or obtain new commands, it will use the Dodge action and preserve itself as best as possible.
	You can use an action to regain concentration on this spell a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge infuses your guardian with energy, allowing it to use an action to cast the elemental surge cantrip as if it were you, only once during the spell's duration, dealing 5d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 99 (Indie)

fields.name: Counter Flood (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell, turning the magic power into healing droplets. If the creature is casting a spell of 4th level or lower, its spell fails and has no effect. If it is casting a spell of 5th level or higher, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the creature's spell fails and has no effect.
	If this effect causes a spell to fail, a creature within range regains a number of hit points equal to 2d8 per spell's level.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can automatically cancel a 5th-level spell slot per level above 7th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 7th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 99 (Indie)

fields.name: Crown of the Sirocco (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Air)
fields.text:
Element: Air

Circles of hot and dry winds surround the targeted creature of this spell, creating a strong wind area with a 10-foot radius around it, granting a +2 bonus to AC and imposing disadvantage on ranged attack rolls made against it. Hostile creatures that start their turn or enter the area must make a Strength saving throw or be pushed out of the area on a failed save.
	During the target's turn, it can use a bonus action to make a ranged spell attack against a creature within 30 feet. If the attack hits, it deals 1d12 bludgeoning damage, and the attacked target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is pushed back 20 feet and fall prone; on a success, it is pushed back 10 feet and remain standing. If there is an obstacle in the way of the pushed creature, it takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was pushed, and if the obstacle is another creature, that creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes the same damage and also fall prone.
	In addition, if a creature is targeted by an attack and the attacker or the target is within 30 feet of the area of this spell, the target can take a reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack by sending a gust of wind towards it.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 99 (Indie)

fields.name: Curse of Flames (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You touch a creature, and it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become cursed for the duration of the spell. The cursed creature feels terrible pain as if it were being burned. Every time you deal damage to the cursed creature, it takes an extra 1d6 fire damage. Additionally, at the start of its turns, the cursed creature must make a Constitution saving throw, and on a failure, the creature feels intense pain and wastes its action of that turn doing nothing.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. If you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration is 8 hours. If you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration is 24 hours. If you use a 9th level spell slot, the spell lasts until it is dispelled. Using a spell slot of 5th level or higher grants a duration that doesn't require concentration.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 99 (Indie)

fields.name: Deflection Air (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You summon the power of wind to protect yourself, preventing damage and even deflecting attacks. For the duration, damage from ranged attacks against you is reduced by an amount equal to 5 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier. If the damage is reduced to 0, you can take a reaction to deflect the attack toward another target within the original range of the attack. When deflecting, you make a ranged spell attack against the new target, applying the original damage to it on a hit.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 100 (Indie)

fields.name: Diamond Sword (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create a magical sword made of pure diamond that rises from the ground. You and any creature who wields the sword are considered proficient with it. The sword's blade is incredibly sharp and is considered to be made of adamantine for damage reduction. In addition, it grants the creature who wields it a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, and any natural roll of 19 or 20 is considered a critical hit. The sword is versatile, able to be used with one hand dealing 2d8 slashing damage or with two hands dealing 2d10 slashing damage, and its damage cannot be healed by any means other than a rest. After the duration, the sword magically disappears.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 11d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 100 (Indie)

fields.name: Disarray Terrain (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You disarrange the terrain in a 20-foot-radius area centered on a point within range. All creatures within the area at the time of its creation must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. After that, the area becomes difficult terrain for the spell's duration. During the spell's duration, you can use your bonus action to shake the disarranged area again, forcing all creatures within it to make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals acid damage, and on the damage roll treat every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 100 (Indie)

fields.name: Disk of Dust (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create a protective barrier in a point of your choice within range, forming a 5-foot-radius circular shield with 2 inches of thickness, made of dust and shimmering energy. The shield has 1d10+10 hit points and provides cover to you and any creatures directly behind it. If the shield hit points reaches 0 it is destroyed, ending the spell.
	While the spell is active, as a bonus action, you can move the shield up to 20 feet in any direction, and even shift it's orientation between vertical and horizontal, but you must remain within 30 feet of it or the spell will end. The shield will block any physical attacks or spells that would pass through it, as any solid barrier, but will not protect against area-of-effect spells or attacks that bypass physical objects.
	In addition, the shield may be used to carry objects up to 50 pounds or activate traps.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the shield's hit points increase by 1d10 for each slot level above 1st.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals acid damage, affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide, on the damage roll treat every 1 or 2 as a 3, and deals an extra 1d6 acid damage for every 2 spell levels used above 1st.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 100 (Indie)

fields.name: Dragon Breath (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You are imbued with the breath of a brass dragon, releasing this breath upon casting and choosing one of the two breaths below:

Fire Breath: You spit out a 60-foot line of fire with a width of 5 feet. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 13d6 fire damage on a failure or half as much damage on a success.

Sleep Breath: You exhale a sleep-inducing gas in a 60-foot cone. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious for 10 minutes. This effect ends if the creature takes damage or another creature uses an action to wake it.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone area, and if you have used the fire breath, you use the sleep breath, but creatures in the area will sleep for 5 minutes. If you have used the sleep breath, you can do a 8d6 fire damage breath, which does not awaken affected creatures.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 100 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Absorption (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You transfer some of the damage that would be caused to you to the earth. When you take damage from any source, you gain resistance to the type of damage that triggered the spell until the end of your next turn.

Elemental Flux: You channel your next elemental surge down your body to your feet and stomp the ground. All creatures in a 10-foot radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 101 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Armor (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small amount of gravel)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create a thin layer of earth around the target and can choose to have one of the two effects below:

	• Grant 1d6 + your Wisdom modifier temporary hit points.

	• The target's base AC becomes 10 + its Dexterity or Constitution modifier (the target chooses the ability to use). If the target is yourself, also add your Wisdom modifier.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals acid damage, and on the damage roll treat every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 101 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Embrace (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 50 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You alter the gravity around up to six creatures of your choice within a 40-foot square within range. Each creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be affected by the spell for the duration.
	An affected creature has difficulty moving and suffers a penalty of -2 to its AC and to its Dexterity and Strength saving throws. Its movement and actions are limited (see below), allowing it to use only half of its movement and only an action or a bonus action on the same turn. The creature cannot maintain concentration on spells and if it attempts to cast a spell, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw; otherwise, the spell fails.

Limited Actions: The targets of the spell have limited but not prevented actions. If a creature wants to take a reaction, or use both its action and bonus action, or use its entire movement, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a success, it can use the chosen option as usual but suffers one level of exhaustion. On a failure, the creature only performs what this spell allows and suffers one level of exhaustion from the effort.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 3d6 acid damage, and if it hits a creature under the effect of earth embrace, it takes double damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 101 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Essence (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You tap into the energy of the earth and are able to perform the following tricks. For this spell, the term earth includes sand, soil, stone, and similar terrains.

	• You can create a small, harmless tremor that extends up to 15 feet in radius and lasts for 1 minute. This can be useful for creating distractions or triggering traps.

	• You can move the earth underneath an object that weighs up to 15 pounds, causing it to move up to 5 feet in any unoccupied direction. This can be helpful for moving small objects or creating obstacles.

	• You can create a small earth construct with an AC of 11, 10 hit points, and 15 feet of movement, up to 25 feet away from you. You can telepathically command the construct to perform simple tasks, such as carrying an object weighing up to 20 pounds. Note that the construct cannot make attacks and will dissolve after 10 minutes or when its hit points are reduced to 0.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 101 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Imprison (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a powder composed of diamond, emerald, ruby, and sapphire dust worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You choose a creature that you can see and that is not native to the Material Plane and trap it within the earth. The chosen creature must make a Charisma saving throw or be swallowed by the earth, becoming trapped in a state of suspended animation underground until released.
	A trapped creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. If the creature accumulates 3 successes, it is freed, but is banished back to its original plane of existence. If it fails 3 times (including the initial one), the creature will remain trapped until it is released by another creature.
	A creature trapped for less than 1001 days that is unearthed exits the state of suspended animation and returns to its plane. A creature that has been trapped for more than 1001 days, when unearthed, is freed from the effects of the spell, but if it dies on the Material Plane within the next 1001 years, it will die permanently and not return to its plane of origin. After these subsequent 1001 days, the creature is free of any effects of this spell. You can release a trapped creature at any time with an action, as long as you are on the same plane of existence.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 102 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Maze (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a miniature maze made of stone)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You make the entire ground tremble in a 60-foot radius centered on you. A number of creatures of your choice, equal to your Wisdom modifier, that you can see within range, are swallowed by the ground, falling into a huge earth maze. Each of the creatures is sent to a different maze, so they can't find each other. To escape the maze, the creature must accumulate 3 successes in Wisdom checks, each of which must be made with their action at the beginning of their next turns. The DC of the Wisdom checks is equal to your spell save DC. For each failure, the creature takes 5d6 bludgeoning damage from small cave-ins in the tunnels. A minotaur or other creature with the Labyrinthine Recall special trait (or a similar one) automatically succeeds on this check.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 12d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 102 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Scales (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

This spell transforms the skin of a creature into stone-like scales. Upon casting, you can choose to grant the target resistance to two of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder, or nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 102 (Indie)

fields.name: Earth Shelter (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Ritual Caster, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

When you touch a silk scarf to a surface of rock or earth, you create a shelter for up to eight people. The entrance marked by the scarf can only be seen by those you designate and is invisible to others. Inside the 20-foot cube shelter is dry, has a comfortable climate, and a small crystal provides illumination that can be turned on or off with a word from anyone chosen. At the end of the spell, you can cast it again to maintain the same shelter, otherwise the spell ends. You can use an action to end the spell at any time, and when the spell ends, the void created fills and expels anything inside it out of it. The volume of available rock or earth must be compatible with the size of the shelter created, otherwise the spell fails.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge imbue the entrance with elemental energy, so that once during the spell's duration, when an undesired person enters the earth shelter, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 5d6 acid damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 102 (Indie)

fields.name: Elemental Frenzy (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite the flames of rage in a creature you can see within range, forcing the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, for the duration of the spell, the creature becomes frenzied and will always attack its nearest creature. If there are no creatures within reach, the affected creature will spend its entire turn moving to the nearest creature. The affected creature is also immune to the frightened and charmed conditions and cannot use spells or any spellcasting abilities, only making armed and unarmed attacks. Additionally, all of its attack rolls will have advantage, but all attack rolls against the affected creature will also have advantage.
	The affected creature can make a new saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break free of the effect on a success. If it has taken any damage since the end of its last turn, it will make the save with disadvantage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge creates a burst, which affects a 10-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 5d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 102 (Indie)

fields.name: Elemental Surge (HB)
fields.text:
With an action, you release pure elemental energy from your hands in a 15-foot cone. You deal 1d6 damage of your primary elemental type, as shown on the table below. All creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking only half damage on a successful save.
	You can also focus all energy on a ray. In this case, you make a ranged spell attack with a range of 60 feet and deal the same damage that it would deal in a cone (or other shapes),
even if empowered by Elemental Flux:

Cantrip Upgrade: This spell's damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Primary Elemental Types:
Primary Element | Damage Type
Air | Thunder
Earth | Acid
Fire | Fire
Water | Cold

At Higher Levels: With this special cantrip, you can expend one of your spell slots to increase the damage it deals. The extra damage added depends on the level of the spell slot used, as shown on the table below. If you use a spell slot of 4th-level or higher, the range of the spell's area of effect doubles (30-foot cone) and if you use a 7th-level or higher spell slot, the range triples (45-foot cone).

Spell Level | Extra Damage
1st | 1d6
2nd | 2d6
3rd | 3d6
4th | 5d6
5th | 6d6
6th | 7d6
7th | 9d6
8th | 10d6
9th | 11d6

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 103 (Indie)

fields.name: Ether Confluence (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You commune with the element of air, and it answers your call. You can determine how the winds of up to 5 miles will behave, accelerating or stopping them. Each round that you accelerate or stop the winds, the winds in the area increase or decrease one stage on the Wind table:

Ether Confluence:
Wind Stage | Condition
1 | Calm
2 | Moderate wind
3 | Strong wind
4 | Gale
5 | Storm

In addition, as a bonus action, you can cause a strong gust of wind to blow in a direction of your choosing, affecting a 120 square feet area. Any creatures that start their turn or enter the area must make a Strength saving throw or be pushed 40 feet in the direction of the wind and be knocked prone. A creature whose movement is impeded by obstructed spaces, such as walls or objects two size categories larger, takes 1d6 damage for every 10 feet it moved before having its movement impeded. If you choose to have the wind blow against the ground or a creature that cannot move due to a wall or other obstructed space caused by large or larger objects, a creature that fails the saving throw is knocked prone and restrained until the beginning of its next turn.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge creates a burst, which affects a 30-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 12d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 103 (Indie)

fields.name: Evanescence of Sue'en (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You connect your essence with that of the air. For the duration, your speed is doubled, you have advantage on any Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, and you don't provoke opportunity attacks for moving.
	In addition, when a creature makes an attack against you, you can take a reaction to dissipate into the air and avoid the attack. While dissipated, you are immune to all damage. At the start of your next turn, you rematerialize in any unoccupied space within 120 feet of the initial point. Creatures of your choice within 5 feet must make a Constitution saving throw, being moved 5 feet and incapacitated for 1 minute on a failure.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 14d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 103 (Indie)

fields.name: Fairy Dance (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You cast this spell and begin to dance, affecting a 30-foot radius sphere centered on you. You can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier to be immune to the effects of this spell, while all other creatures that start their turn or enter the area and can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they are charmed. A creature charmed by this spell begins to replicate your dance.
	While you use your action to dance, all charmed creatures dance along with you, losing their actions. If you move, the creatures move with you in the best way they can, expending their movement on their next turn. A creature that is more than 60 feet away from you, or who fails to see you for two turns or takes damage, is freed from the spell's effects.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 104 (Indie)
